$comment: Model routing policy (architecture §6, claude-in-dcc §6.3/§8.3/§9.9). Config-as-code: this is the GLOBAL layer; client-level overrides deep-merge on top. Every call to Claude declares its capability; route() picks a tier, effort and cap from here, and the decision is written on the call's ledger row together with `version`, so a cost change can be tied to a policy edit. The router is rules, not a model. escalateOn/downgradeOn are lists: ANY entry matching triggers (keys within one entry are AND). Edited from the control center (מדיניות ושמירה), which bumps `version` and records who changed it.

prices.$comment: USD per million tokens, Anthropic's list prices as of 2026-09. The CLI reports each call's cost itself; the ledger keeps the price-list version so a cost can be recomputed from its tokens.

capabilities.$comment: A capability nothing calls is a statement, not a policy — every key here has a caller, and the control center shows how many calls each one had this month.
capabilities.$onboarding_comment: The onboarding session is Claude Code's own /init, run once per repository; what it writes steers every later session there for months, so it gets a strong default. A person can change model and effort per run, or type /model and /effort in the session itself. Its cost is recorded as ledger slices, one per stage of the run.
capabilities.$chat_comment: The one chat. It answers from the facts the screen hands it; step zero answers glossary and fact questions with no call at all. Haiku, no thinking, short answers. A call whose input passes maxInputTokens is refused and recorded — the sign that the delta discipline broke.
capabilities.$interactive_comment: A person's own Claude Code session, reported by the SessionEnd hook — recorded so the ledger is every call, never routed.

chat.$comment: Opening values (claude-in-dcc §6.5, §6.6, §9.10); tuned by measurement in the control center, not by estimate (§6.8).
